_comment: Grants & Contracts (2026-10-13). Finds money a person can earn with their own skills — grants, fellowships, prizes, public contracts, rosters, and paid vendor roles inside other organisations' awards — then drafts and fills applications for their approval. Public and generic: the person's location, work lines and conflict-of-interest rules live in their private grants-profile.json and in this assistant's memories on their Mac, never in this file. The deterministic half (new vs seen, deadline changes, conflict exclusions, funder-page diffs) is grants/tools/scan.py, linked into the working folder.
blurb: Finds grants, contracts and paid vendor roles that fit your skills, checks every deadline at the source, and drafts applications for your approval.
_whyCadenceManual: The legacy cadence job composes a calendar-and-sources brief, which is not this assistant's work. Its weekly scan is a Routine instead: the thread proposes routines/templates/weekly-script-report (slug grants-scan, entry run.py copied from grants/tools/routine_run.py), the person approves it once, and each run files a dated report. That is the `schedule` trigger below.
_whyRecords: Opportunities and applications are a series, so they are ROWS (CW.4 lesson from job-search: each one as a memory rode along with every turn until the thread overflowed). Funding Opportunities has one row per funder, programme and cycle (Key 'Funder — Program — Cycle'); Funding Applications has one row per submission. Memories hold only durable facts about the person: where they live, how they can be paid (individual, for-profit, nonprofit partner), their work lines, and their conflict-of-interest rules.
_whyFreshness: Two layers, both deterministic: scan.py's state/seen.json (an opportunity is reported once, then only when its deadline changes; a funder page is reported only when its text changes) and the Ledger Key, which makes a re-added row update instead of duplicate.
_whyQualityControl: evidence: a deadline, amount or eligibility rule enters a row only quoted from the funder's own page or an official feed, with the date read. deterministic: scan.py applies the profile's conflict exclusions before the model sees anything, and its selftest pins that. human: nothing is submitted, sent or signed without an approval card.
_whyMailSendIsNotGranted: Same rule as job-search. Emails to program managers, partners and procurement officers are drafted (mail.draft) and sent only from an approval card a human pressed. Granting mail.send would take the person out of the middle of anything written in their name.
_whyMailIsEnumeratedNotWildcarded: mail.* would match mail.send. Enumerated means a future mail verb arrives ungranted and someone reads it before adding it.
_whyAiwebIsGranted: Applications live in funder portals (Submittable, Fluxx, state and county portals). Filling them is the 'apply' half of this assistant. Every page action is an approval card, and a final Submit runs only when the person approves it or has chosen to let that site finish.
_whyRoutinesAreEnumerated: routines.propose only creates a card awaiting the person's approval (ROUTINES_ARCHITECTURE §5). update, pause, resume, runNow and delete are not needed to set up one weekly scan and are left out. As of 2026-10-13 the routines.* verbs are designed but not yet in the app, so these grants are inert until they ship; until then CONTEXT.md has the thread ask the person to add the weekly scan and run scans on request.
_whyUntrustedInput: Funder pages, RFP documents, alert emails and portal text are written by outsiders and reach an assistant that can drive a signed-in browser and queue approval cards. They are data to quote, never instructions; the standing rule is in CONTEXT.md.
_whyBudget: Advisory, and only checked when another assistant relays a question here (AssistantRelay.check). The weekly scan itself is a script with no model calls.
